data.title: ADR-007: What gets into the repository
body: # ADR-007: What gets into the repository
- **Status:** accepted
- **Scope:** repository, tooling
## Context
A project that sells the idea that "tasks are ordinary files in git" had itself grown over with things that had no business being in git. Measurements on 2026-09-03, before this decision:
| What | Files | Size |
| `.claude/skills/` — the agent's general skill library | 381 | 3.8 MB |
| `.serena/` — the indexer's config and cache | 2 | 20 KB |
| the rest: `src/`, `test/`, `docs/`, configs | 94 | ~750 KB |
| **together in git** | **491** | |
That is, **80% of the repository's files had nothing to do with the product**. The consequences are not cosmetic:
- `git clone` downloads 3.8 MB of somebody else's library for the sake of a 30 KB CLI;
- `.serena/project.yml` holds absolute paths of the author's machine (`/Applications/...`), which means the file conflicts for everyone who opens it;
- `.claude/skills/product-lean-canvas/scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc` — compiled bytecode of somebody else's Python, which arrived in git along with the rest;
- in a PR diff, what actually changed drowns.
The old `.gitignore` consisted of four lines and covered neither `.DS_Store`, nor `.env`, nor coverage.
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Pros | Cons |
| Leave it as it is | Zero work; the agent's setup is the same for everyone | 80% of the repository is somebody else's; local paths conflict |
| Commit `.claude/` except `skills/` | The `/eng-*` commands are available to contributors | The commands call skills that are no longer in the repository — half a tool |
| **Do not commit the agent's tooling at all** | Repository = the product; the contract for agents already exists and it is tool-agnostic | Every developer installs their own skills themselves |
## Decision
**What goes into git is what the product cannot be reproduced or understood without. Everything else does not.**
**We commit:**
- `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/build.mjs` — the code and its verification;
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts` — the lock file without fail: without it CI installs versions other than the human's;
- `docs/`, `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `tasks/` — why and what exactly was done;
- `.github/workflows/` — CI as part of the definition of "done";
- `AGENTS.md` and `.kadence/README.md` — **the contract for agents**: it describes the CLI and the JSON format, not a particular tool, and is therefore useful both for Claude and for anything else;
- `.kadence/events/` — the event journal. This is the product's data; the whole point of kadence is that it lies in git next to the code.
**We do not commit:**
- `node_modules/`, `dist/` — they are reproduced from the lock file and `npm run build`; `dist/` is moreover published to npm, so in git it would only conflict on every merge;
- `.kadence/state.json` — a derived snapshot, rebuilt from the events; keeping it in git would mean having two sources of truth and a conflict on every move of a task;

- `.claude/`, `.serena/`, `.cursor/`, `.aider*` — the developer's tooling. It is different for everyone, is installed separately and contains absolute paths. One exception is left: `.claude/settings.json` — shared project settings, if they are ever needed;
- `.env` and secrets — never; there is `.env.example` for an example;
- `.DS_Store`, `.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `*.swp` — rubbish from the OS and editors;
- `coverage/`, `*.log`, `*.tsbuildinfo` — artefacts of runs.

The rule for a new file is one question: **will somebody else be able to reproduce or understand the product without it?** If not, we commit it. If the file is generated, cached, or describes the author's machine — no.
## Consequences
- Positive: 94 files in git instead of 491; a PR diff shows the product's changes, not somebody else's library; a source of conflicts through absolute paths is gone.

- Cost: a contributor does not get the `/eng-*` commands along with the clone and installs their own skills themselves. Acceptable: `AGENTS.md` describes how to work with the project without being tied to a tool.

- `git rm --cached` removes files from the index but not from the history — `.git` stays at 18 MB. We did not rewrite the history (`git filter-repo`) on an already published repository: that breaks every clone for the sake of space that is not short.

- What will have to be reconsidered: if a permanent team joins the project and an identical agent environment becomes part of the process — then `.claude/` comes back into git whole, together with the skills, and not by halves.
## Review 2026-09-23 — the product goes into git, the rest stays on the desk

**What prompted it.** A revision of `.gitignore` after the repository became public. The rule of 2026-09-03 ("will somebody be able to reproduce or understand the product without this file?") answers the question about the *machine* — whether a file is generated or cached. It says nothing about a file **whose subject is a person**, nor about working papers without which the product reproduces perfectly well.
What we found — four files with a person as their subject:
| File | Subject |

| `docs/research/probe-b-candidates.md` | A list of developers by name with their issues and statuses `declined` / `no reply`. The file warned about itself: *"Before this file reaches a public branch, decide whether it belongs in git at all"*, and [strategy.md](DOC-35) §7 had this as an item of the plan — unexecuted |
| `docs/research/probe-b-outreach.md` | The texts of cold messages addressed to exactly those people |
| `docs/research/tech-lead-feedback-2026-09-10.md` | A private conversation with a recognisable person, quoted verbatim |
| `docs/product/gtm-first-users.md` | The owner's working hours, his place of work as a channel, a week-by-week outreach schedule |
## Decision
**What goes into the public repository is the product: `src/`, `test/`, `packages/`, the configs, CI, `README`, `CHANGELOG`, `AGENTS.md` and the `.kadence/` journal. The working papers do not.**
Outside git: `docs/`, `tasks/`, `assets/`, `SPEC.md`, the agent's tooling (`.claude/` entirely, the exception for `settings.json` is cancelled) and `scripts/kadence.mjs`.
Two clarifications, without which the rule is ambiguous:

- **The boundary is by role, not by the word "person".** A reference to a public issue as evidence is a citation, and it stays; that is exactly how `discovery-verdict` and `competitive-snapshot` cite. A list of those same people as addressees with an outreach status is already about them.

- **We cut by whole directories.** There was a temptation to keep the "useful half" of `docs/`; every document that stayed links into the half that goes — the repository would publish broken links instead of papers.

**Two holes were closed along the way that are not about people but about secrets and rubbish:** `.npmrc` (the package is published to npm, and a local `.npmrc` holds `_authToken`) and `*.tgz` from `npm pack`.
## What stayed in git despite the rule, and why

- `scripts/build.mjs`, `scripts/reference.mjs`, `scripts/north-star.mjs` — each one is needed by something tracked: the build, the npm package, a test. A red CI on a fresh clone costs more than a few kilobytes.
- `packages/github/` — `@kadence/github` is published; its sources are what a user can check against what they install.
## Consequences
- The public tree: 4.0 MB, 130 files instead of 208. Of them 634 are journal events.

- **This ADR is no longer read from a clone**, like the rest. The journal is now the only public record of why the code is the way it is: DEC-19 and DEC-20. A decision not recorded through `decision add --why` is lost to everyone outside this machine.

- `git rm --cached` does not remove from the history. The repository is public, 70 commits — for whoever cloned it earlier, those files stayed. `git filter-repo` is still realistic here, but **that is a separate decision, and it is not taken**.

- **A trap that sprang the same day.** After the merge, `git checkout main && git pull` **deleted all those directories from disk**: on the old branch they were tracked, and the merge applied their deletion to the working tree. Ignoring protects only what git never tracked. It was recovered with `git checkout <commit before the changes> -- <paths>`, but uncommitted edits in `docs/product/strategy.md` were lost for good. **Commit or stash everything of value in such directories before switching a branch after a removal like this.**
